member.name: T:HumanGateway.Relay.Services.RelaySyncService
member.summary:
The Relay's sync engine driver (RELAY-FR-02, SYNC-FR-01..07): applies inbound PUSH batches from registered gateways and serves their PULL requests, consuming the shared contract for cursor math, idempotency, deterministic ordering, and delivery acknowledgements. The service owns the cross-school routing side effect (product vision §6.3, RELAY-FR-04): applied messages are routed to the recipient gateways' pull queues (the relay_outbox), and delivery acknowledgements (SYNC-FR-05) flow back to the sender through the same queue — both schools only ever talk to the Relay (SP-01).
Delivery is at-least-once end to end; exactly-once effect comes from idempotency on both sides (NF-05): batch idempotency at the Relay (the engine's ), per-message dedup, and the durable pull cursor the Edge echoes back. Routing and ack application are re-run on a replayed batch — every side effect here is idempotent — so a retry after a partial failure converges without duplication.

This is the inbound (Relay → gateway) stream, driven by the sync engine's BuildPushBatchAsync when the gateway pulls. Sequence allocation is a single atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ...
